title: Acid-Base Titration Curves: Structure, Concentration, and pH During Acid-Base Titration
assignedQuestion: How do acid/base strength and concentration affect the shape and landmarks of a pH-volume titration curve?

combinations.label: Known strong acid vs known strong base
Unknown weak acid vs known strong base
Unknown weak base vs known strong acid

probeRules: Rinse the probe with deionized water before and between samples; blot gently without wiping the bulb.
Calibrate with the teacher-specified buffers before the first formal run.
Keep the sensing bulb immersed without touching the vessel or stir bar.
Wait for the configured stability criterion before reading, then record pH separately.

hazardSummary: Acids and bases can damage skin and eyes; review the teacher-provided SDS information for every assigned sample.
Some concentrated acids are extremely corrosive and hygroscopic.
safety.spillResponse: Report spills immediately. If solution contacts skin, rinse with running water for 15 minutes and notify the instructor.
safety.dilutionRule: When dilution is authorized, add acid to water. Never add water to concentrated acid.
safety.disposalProcedure: Neutralize collected waste, test its pH, and dispose only by the instructor's posted procedure.
